rv.q: This is the rarest of things: a Dream the whole family can enjoy.
Lim and her cast made it come alive for me again.

Now, then, for some light relief and a reminder of how silly the play’s high jinks can be. Emily Lim’s take is frivolous, folksy and fun – and family-friendly, too. It takes a butterfly approach to its themes, fluttering briefly over each, then moving to the next.
So if you’re thinking of going to this production to get your little one started early on some culture then surely that should be enough to recommend it?
This version of Dream is something close to a folk musical, with original songs by Jim Fortune.
And this one is a glorious riot of colour and confusion.
It’s a Dream that’s very much in the Globe’s tradition of crowd-pleasing entertainment, filled with music, laughter, and appropriately absurd audience participation.
Lim’s production is bright and big on spectacle, making it brilliantly accessible to new audiences both young and old.
It’s just one of a number of ingenious little twists that make this a genuinely joyous, energetic and celebratory interpretation.

cn.t: Critics praise this joyful, crowd-pleasing production for its vibrant energy, playful audience participation, and gloriously colorful design. The folky, accessible approach delights families and newcomers, though purists may find it too irreverent.
